title: D-Wave launched quantum simulator beta program
key_facts: D-Wave Quantum announced a beta programme for its gate-model quantum computing simulator
A limited set of customers get early access before general release
Aim is to let them try error-aware programming ahead of D-Wave's upcoming gate-model hardware
Simulator is based on D-Wave's dual-rail superconducting gate-model technology, which the company says is designed for error detection and efficient error correction
Participants include BBVA, FirstQFM, Florida Atlantic University and the Julich Supercomputing Centre
CEO Alan Baratz called it a major step in executing the roadmap
quote_evidence: D-Wave announced the initiation of a beta programme for its gate-model quantum computing simulator.
Quantum error correction is a defining challenge in the race to commercially useful gate-model quantum computing, said CEO Alan Baratz.
why_it_matters_hint: A software preview, not hardware: the gate-model machine it prepares for is still upcoming.
